description: Surface environment at Jezero crater, the Mars Sandbox v0.1 region. Primary source is Perseverance MEDA. Values marked approx need to be re-derived from the PDS MEDA archive by the coding agent (see AGENT_BRIEF.md task F2).

facts.label: Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
facts.notes: Jezero is a ~50 km crater on the NW rim of the Isidis basin; Noachian lake basin with a fluvial delta.

facts.label: Elevation of landing site (MOLA datum)

uncertainty.note: approx; re-derive from MOLA MEGDR 128 ppd at the landing coordinates

facts.notes: Superseded by the value sampled from the MEGDR tile in task T1; kept per the replace-do-not-overwrite rule.

facts.label: Elevation of landing site, MOLA MEGDR 128 ppd (areoid datum)

uncertainty.note: spread of the 3x3 bilinear samples (460 m spacing) around the site; MEGDR bins near the equator are interpolated across up to 12 km profile gaps

facts.notes: Bilinear sample of MEGT44N000HB.IMG (product version 2.0) at jezero.location.landing_site by terrain/mola_jezero.py; reproduced by web/terrain/jezero_mola_40km.json (elevation_m.centre). Height above the GMM3 areoid per the PDS label. Superseded by the 1 m HiRISE DTM sample, which it agrees with to within its own 3x3 spread.

facts.label: Elevation of landing site, USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE DTM mosaic (MOLA areoid datum)

uncertainty.note: spread of the 3x3 samples at 1 m spacing; the mosaic's absolute tie to MOLA is through the CTX DTM (see source lineage), so expect metre-level absolute error

facts.instrument: MRO HiRISE stereo (USGS SOCET SET DTM, MOLA-controlled)
facts.notes: Bilinear sample of JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40.tif at jezero.location.landing_site by terrain/hirise_jezero.py; reproduced by web/terrain/jezero_hirise_5km.json (elevation_m.centre).

facts.label: Terrain data products for the v0.1 region
facts.value: MOLA MEGDR 128 ppd (global, ~463 m/px) + HiRISE 1 m/px stereo DTM over the Perseverance field site
facts.notes: Stack et al. 2020 mapped the field site at 1:5000 on a 25 cm/px HiRISE orthomosaic and 1 m/px DTM. Task T1 uses the USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE DTM mosaic (usgs-m2020-hirise-dtm, 1 m/px) for the playable region and MOLA MEGDR for the crater-scale context; the Stack et al. supplementary record offers no DTM download.

Surface pressure envelope over a Mars year

uncertainty.note: approx envelope; driven by the seasonal CO2 polar-cap cycle (~±8%) plus a diurnal thermal-tide cycle of a few percent

facts.notes: APPROX. Agent task F2: replace with min/max/mean from the PDS MEDA PS archive for MY36.

facts.label: Mean near-surface air temperature over a Mars year (1.45 m)
facts.notes: Reported as 'around minus 55 degrees Celsius' averaged across seasons.

facts.label: Typical nightly minimum air temperature
Typical afternoon maximum air temperature
facts.notes: APPROX. Ground (not air) temperature at midday can approach or exceed 273 K in summer; the ground-air difference is large on Mars because the air is so thin. Agent task F2.

facts.label: Typical day-night air temperature swing
facts.notes: This swing, not the mean, is what kills unheated structures. A thermal-mass design must bridge it every sol.

facts.label: Surface thermal inertia along the traverse
facts.notes: Low values = loose dust/sand (fast heating and cooling); high = bedrock. Matters for regolith-as-insulation designs.

facts.label: Broadband surface albedo (0.3-3 um)

uncertainty.note: varies with illumination angle; minimum near noon

facts.label: Typical visible dust optical depth (clear season)

uncertainty.note: approx; Jezero was reported clearer than Gale at landing

facts.notes: APPROX. Surface irradiance ≈ TOA * exp(-tau/cos(sza)) * (scattering correction). Agent task F2: pull the Mastcam-Z tau series.

facts.label: Peak visible optical depth, regional dust storm 5-11 Jan 2022 (Ls 153-156)
facts.notes: A regional storm roughly quarters usable solar power for days. Global storms (2018 killed Opportunity) can reach tau ~8-10 and last months; none has been measured at Jezero yet.

facts.label: Dust devil frequency of occurrence (first 365 sols)
facts.notes: Peak 12:00-13:00 LTST. Dust devils at Jezero can exceed 100 m diameter. A dust devil damaged a MEDA wind sensor in the Jan 2022 storm. Relevant to solar panel dust loading (also cleaning events).

facts.label: Estimated GCR dose equivalent at Jezero

uncertainty.note: scaled from Gale measurement for ~1.9 km less atmospheric shielding and solar-cycle variation

facts.notes: Rule of thumb: ~1 m of regolith or ~2-3 m of water reduces GCR dose substantially; shielding is a design parameter, not a fact. Agent: model, do not state as measured.

facts.label: Likelihood of accessible water ice in the top 5 m at Jezero latitude (18 N)
facts.notes: SWIM maps show consistent shallow ice mostly poleward of ~35-40 deg latitude. Jezero is a science site, not a resource site. Water for a Jezero base is therefore hydrated minerals, atmospheric extraction, or import. This is a design constraint the agent must surface.

facts.label: Liquid water in fractured mid-crust (global inference from InSight)

uncertainty.note: single-site seismic inversion; authors argue it is likely global

facts.notes: Volume exceeds proposed ancient oceans. Not accessible with any plausible drilling; relevant to astrobiology scenarios, not to base water supply.

facts.label: Depth below which diurnal temperature swing is negligible

uncertainty.note: depends on thermal inertia; the annual wave penetrates several metres

facts.formula: skin depth d = sqrt(2*kappa/omega), kappa from thermal inertia and regolith density
facts.notes: Agent must compute this from the primitives library, not hard-code it. Buried or regolith-covered structures see the mean (~218 K), not the swing.
